2027 Hyundai Elantra Officially Unveiled in Los Angeles: It's Longer, Wider, Taller, Smarter
11 photos
Photo: Hyundai
While SUVs and pickup trucks get all the attention in America, Hyundai proves that sedans are still alive with the all-new Elantra, one of the best-selling models in the segment in the U.S. Here comes the all-new, eighth-generation Hyundai Elantra, alongside the 2028 Elantra Hybrid. Both were unveiled at the Los Angeles Auto Show, just miles from the brand’s U.S. headquarters.
They call it Elantra, i30, and Avante . Its name depends on who you ask and where you buy it from. Regardless of the name, the model has been completely redesigned. It grew in all directions, it got a sharper look, and it received new tech.
The eighth-generation 2027 Hyundai Elantra is significantly larger than the outgoing model, stretching 3.4 inches (85 millimeters) longer, 1.2 inches (30 millimeters) wider, 0.4 inches (10 millimeters) taller, and riding on a 1.2-inch longer wheelbase, which translates to more legroom, shoulder room, and headroom for those sitting in the back.
In the meantime, the Elantra is keeping its exterior footprint in the compact class, where it is ready to give the Toyota Corolla and the Honda Civic a run for their money in the compact sedan segment in the United States.
Photo: Hyundai The car follows Hyundai's new "Art of Steel" design language. The redesigned silhouette trades the previous generation’s soft curves for sharper lines, muscular fenders, and flush-mounted door handles. It all starts with the H-shaped LED lighting signature at both ends, something that we first saw in the Hyundai Santa Fe SUV .
The new Hyundai Elantra gets the firm’s new Android Automotive OS-based infotainment system, Pleos Connect, running on a standard 12.9-inch central touchscreen. It supports over-the-air updates, wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, and the optional LLM-powered voice assistant called Gleo AI.
Yet, the model retains something that other automakers are returning to after years of transferring all functions to touchscreens. The 2027 Hyundai Elantra and 2028 Elantra Hybrid will get physical climate and audio knobs, as executives say driving the sedan is an "eyes on the road, hands on the wheel" experience.
The slim digital instrument cluster sits near the base of the windshield, displaying relevant driving data. The gearbox shifter migrated to the steering column, freeing up space in the center console for dual wireless charging pads. The options list includes a Bang & Olufsen sound system and second-row air vents.
Photo: Hyundai The powertrain of the new generation won’t make headlines. The 2027 Hyundai Elantra retains the naturally aspirated 2.0-liter Smartstream inline-four and Intelligent Variable Transmission ( IVT ), producing 147 horsepower (149 metric horsepower) and 132 pound-feet (179 Newton meters) of torque. An N variant should arrive at a later date with more oomph, but nope, Hyundai isn't planning an Elantra station wagon .
In the meantime, the 2028 Elantra Hybrid will come with the 1.6-liter inline four and an electric motor for a combined output of 155 horsepower (157 metric horsepower). Hyundai hasn't disclosed the torque figure of the hybrid Elantra yet. A six-speed dual-clutch transmission puts the power down. Both powetrains operate in a front-wheel-drive setup.
The price has yet to be announced. Hyundai will disclose the missing numbers closer to the launch date. To keep the Elantra competitive in the United States, Hyundai will have to position it very close to its main rivals in the compact segment: the Toyota Corolla starts at $23,125, while the Corolla Hybrid is a $24,975 deal. In the meantime, the Honda Civic kicks off at $24,695 and the Civic Hybrid is a $29,395 deal.
